samples.title: Build & Deliver: Plan a Toy Route
samples.description: Build, test, and improve a route before making one final pretend delivery.
samples.goal: Plan and improve a route while solving simple problems about space and movement.

guestPreview.imageAlt: Wooden blocks arranged as roads for small toy cars.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Keep the route on the floor and away from doorways or stairs.

missions.title: Gather the route pieces
setupSteps: Place two cushions on the floor.
Add a few blocks and one spoon or toy car.
missions.sayThis: A delivery is waiting. What kind of road should we build?
missions.childChallenge: Choose where the delivery route begins and ends.
missions.tidyUp: Keep unused blocks in their basket.

missions.title: Build bridges and bends
setupSteps: Use blocks to mark two bends.
Make one cushion into a gentle bridge.
missions.sayThis: Can the driver find a way over the bridge?
missions.childChallenge: Test the route, then change one part to make it easier or trickier.
missions.tidyUp: Move any loose pieces away from walking paths.

missions.title: Make the final delivery
setupSteps: Choose a small soft item as the parcel.
Put it at the starting point.
missions.sayThis: Who needs this special delivery today?
missions.childChallenge: Carry the parcel along the whole route and invent who receives it.
missions.tidyUp: Return cushions and blocks together when the delivery is complete.

samples.title: Kitchen Shadow Safari: Explore Light & Stories
samples.description: Change the size and shape of shadows, discover creatures, and tell their story.
samples.goal: Explore how light and distance change shadows, then turn those observations into a story.

guestPreview.imageAlt: Warm torchlight casting playful shadows from kitchen tools.
guestPreview.safetyNote: An adult holds the torch. Do not shine it toward anyone's eyes.

missions.title: Find a shadow den
setupSteps: Dim one room slightly.
Point the torch at a clear wall from arm's length.
missions.sayThis: Our wall is a quiet jungle. Who might be hiding here?
missions.childChallenge: Move closer and farther from the wall to change the shadow size.
missions.tidyUp: Keep the floor clear while the room is dim.

missions.title: Discover three creatures
setupSteps: Hold a slotted spoon or colander between the torch and wall.
missions.sayThis: What animal does this shadow remind you of?
missions.childChallenge: Name three shadow creatures and show how each one moves.
missions.tidyUp: Place each kitchen tool on a nearby table after using it.

missions.title: Tell the safari story
setupSteps: Choose the child's favourite shadow creature.
missions.sayThis: Where is our creature going before bedtime?
missions.childChallenge: Tell a beginning, middle, and ending for the creature's adventure.
missions.tidyUp: Turn on the room light before returning the torch and tools.

samples.title: Rainbow Route Challenge: Listen, Remember & Move
samples.description: Follow short colour directions, remember the route, and become the leader who guides a grown-up.
samples.goal: Help your child follow two- and three-step directions, remember a sequence, and plan one for you.

guestPreview.imageAlt: Colourful paper stepping stones arranged as an indoor movement trail.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Tape paper flat on a dry floor and keep the trail away from stairs and sharp furniture.

background.alt: A colourful Rainbow Trail Mission Wall

missions.title: Learn the colour route
setupSteps: Lay the coloured sheets in a gentle curve.
Tape each corner flat.
missions.sayThis: Let's name the colours in order as we walk the route together.
missions.childChallenge: Choose the colour order, walk it once, and say each colour aloud.
missions.tidyUp: Press down any paper edge that starts to lift.

missions.title: Listen and remember
setupSteps: Stand beside the route where every colour is easy to see.
missions.sayThis: Listen first: blue, yellow. Can you visit those colours in that order?
missions.childChallenge: Follow two two-colour directions, then try one three-colour direction without a reminder.
missions.tidyUp: Pause and retape any sheet that starts to move.

missions.title: Become the route leader
setupSteps: Let the child stand where they can see the whole route.
missions.sayThis: Now you are the leader. Which three colours should I visit, and in what order?
missions.childChallenge: Create a three-step colour direction, say it clearly, and check whether the grown-up follows it.
missions.tidyUp: Peel up the tape slowly and stack the paper for another day.

samples.title: Pillow Animal Rescue: Move, Care & Pretend
samples.description: Build a safe route, rescue toy animals with care, and prepare their cosy home.
samples.goal: Move carefully through a simple route while creating a caring rescue story.

guestPreview.imageAlt: Soft cushions making a rescue route for small toy animals.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Keep cushions flat on the floor and use only soft, lightweight toys.

background.alt: A cosy animal rescue Mission Wall

missions.title: Make a safe rescue path
setupSteps: Place three cushions in a short line.
Put the basket at the far end.
missions.sayThis: Our animals need a safe path home. Where should it go?
missions.childChallenge: Arrange the cushions and test the path with one careful walk.
missions.tidyUp: Move any hard toys away from the path.

missions.title: Rescue each animal
setupSteps: Place one toy animal beside the first cushion and one beside the last.
missions.sayThis: What does each animal need on the journey?
missions.childChallenge: Carry each animal across while copying the way it moves.
missions.tidyUp: Return each rescued animal to the basket.

missions.title: Prepare the cosy home
setupSteps: Use one cushion beside the basket as a soft roof.
missions.sayThis: How will the animals know they are safely home?
missions.childChallenge: Make a welcome sound and tell a short ending to the rescue story.
missions.tidyUp: Put the animals away and return the cushions together.

samples.title: Kitchen Rhythm Parade: Copy & Create Beats
samples.description: Listen to a simple beat, copy its pattern, and create one for a home parade.
samples.goal: Listen, remember, and create simple rhythm patterns while moving together.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A wooden spoon, bowl, and scarf ready for a gentle kitchen rhythm parade.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Use a plastic bowl, tap gently, and keep the parade route clear.

missions.title: Find a gentle beat
setupSteps: Turn the plastic bowl upside down.
Hold the wooden spoon loosely.
missions.sayThis: Can we make a quiet beat that sounds like walking feet?
missions.childChallenge: Tap four slow beats, pause, then repeat them.
missions.tidyUp: Keep the spoon resting beside the bowl between turns.

missions.title: Copy the rhythm
setupSteps: Choose a two-beat pattern together.
missions.sayThis: I will tap a pattern. Can you echo it back?
missions.childChallenge: Copy two patterns, then invent one for the grown-up to copy.
missions.tidyUp: Use soft taps so the bowl stays in place.

missions.title: Lead the tiny parade
setupSteps: Hold the scarf as a parade flag.
Choose a short clear route.
missions.sayThis: Where should our music parade travel?
missions.childChallenge: March the route while humming the beat, then finish with a quiet bow.
missions.tidyUp: Return the bowl and spoon, then fold the scarf.

samples.title: Nature Detective Lab: Find Patterns & Explain Why
samples.description: Look for evidence, test two ways of grouping the same objects, and challenge a grown-up with a secret rule.
samples.goal: Practise early science and maths by comparing objects in different ways and explaining the rule used.

guestPreview.imageAlt: Leaves, smooth stones, and seed pods arranged in a simple sorting tray.
guestPreview.safetyNote: A grown-up chooses clean, non-toxic items that are too large to swallow; wash hands afterward.

background.alt: A calm nature detective Mission Wall

missions.title: Collect the evidence
setupSteps: Spread the cloth on a table or floor.
Place the tray and nature finds on top.
missions.sayThis: Detectives look closely. What is one detail you can see or feel on each object?
missions.childChallenge: Inspect every object and describe at least one clue about its colour, shape, size, or texture.
missions.tidyUp: Keep every nature find on the cloth.

missions.title: Test two pattern rules
setupSteps: Put the bowls or tray sections within easy reach.
missions.sayThis: Can the same objects belong to different groups when we change the rule?
missions.childChallenge: Group the objects by one rule, explain it, then mix them up and choose a completely different rule.
missions.tidyUp: Return mixed items to the middle before starting the next sort.

missions.title: Create a secret rule
setupSteps: Ask the grown-up to look away while the child makes two groups.
missions.sayThis: Make a secret sorting rule. I will study your evidence and try to guess it.
missions.childChallenge: Sort the objects using a secret rule, listen to the grown-up's guess, then explain the evidence that proves the answer.
missions.tidyUp: Return outdoor items responsibly and wash hands together.

samples.title: Jump the Secret Code: Look, Move & Remember
samples.description: Follow a tiny floor code with your feet, remember it, and invent a new route for a grown-up.
samples.goal: Turn a simple tape path into a playful challenge for attention, balance, and working memory.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A short tape path of circles with different foot-position lines.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Make a short path on a dry floor away from furniture and stairs. Remove tape slowly afterward.

missions.title: Build a three-move code
setupSteps: Tape three circles or squares in a short line.
Add one straight line inside each shape in a different direction.
missions.sayThis: Each mark is a secret instruction for our feet.
missions.childChallenge: Step into each shape and turn both feet to match its line.
missions.tidyUp: Press down any loose tape edge before moving.

missions.title: Remember the route
setupSteps: Look at all three marks together.
Start one step before the first shape.
missions.sayThis: Can your feet remember the whole code without stopping?
missions.childChallenge: Travel the route twice, then try once while looking toward the finish.
missions.tidyUp: Pause if the floor or tape starts to slip.

missions.title: Become the code maker
setupSteps: Let the child point to a new order for the three shapes.
missions.sayThis: You made the code. Can I solve it?
missions.childChallenge: Guide a grown-up through the route and spot one funny mistake.
missions.tidyUp: Peel up the tape slowly and roll it into one small ball.

samples.title: Wake the Paper Worms: Colour, Predict & Watch
samples.description: Make tiny paper worms, predict what water will do, and watch them uncurl together.
samples.goal: Create a quick transformation that encourages fine-motor control, prediction, and close observation.

guestPreview.imageAlt: Colourful rolled paper worms beginning to uncurl on a plate.
materials: plate with a spoonful of water
guestPreview.safetyNote: An adult handles the water and prepares the tight paper rolls. The worms are for play, not eating.

missions.title: Draw the worm stripes
setupSteps: Tear three narrow tissue strips.
Draw spaced stripes across each strip with washable markers.
missions.sayThis: Which two colours should your first worm wear?
missions.childChallenge: Give each strip a different repeating colour pattern.
missions.tidyUp: Keep marker caps together beside the plate.

missions.title: Make the worms sleep
setupSteps: An adult rolls each strip around a marker and gently pushes the ends together.
Slide each compressed roll onto the dry plate.
missions.sayThis: Which sleeping worm do you think will stretch the farthest?
missions.childChallenge: Choose a prediction and explain what you noticed about that worm.
missions.tidyUp: Put the markers away before adding water.

missions.title: Wake them with water
setupSteps: Spoon a little water around the worms without covering them.
missions.sayThis: Watch closely—what changes first?
missions.childChallenge: Describe how each worm moves and check whether the prediction was right.
missions.tidyUp: Place the damp tissue in the bin and wipe the plate.

samples.title: Sock Parcel Toss: Aim, Adjust & Deliver
samples.description: Turn rolled socks into parcels, aim for a laundry-basket town, and improve each delivery route.
samples.goal: Practise aiming and force control while making simple decisions about distance and difficulty.

guestPreview.imageAlt: Rolled sock parcels beside a laundry-basket delivery target.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Use only soft rolled socks, clear the throwing area, and aim away from people and breakable objects.

missions.title: Prepare the soft parcels
setupSteps: Roll three pairs of socks into soft balls.
Place the basket two big steps away.
missions.sayThis: These parcels need careful drivers.
missions.childChallenge: Choose a pretend item inside each parcel and name its destination.
missions.tidyUp: Keep every parcel at the starting point.

missions.title: Find the best throw
setupSteps: Throw underarm from the starting point.
missions.sayThis: Was that throw too soft, too strong, or just right?
missions.childChallenge: Deliver all three parcels, changing the next throw after every miss.
missions.tidyUp: Collect missed parcels only after all three throws.

missions.title: Choose a new delivery route
setupSteps: Move the basket one step nearer, farther, or sideways.
missions.sayThis: How did the new route change your plan?
missions.childChallenge: Complete one final round and explain which position was easiest.
missions.tidyUp: Return the socks to the basket together.

samples.title: Feed the Colour Creatures: Match, Post & Switch
samples.description: Make three hungry paper creatures, feed them matching cards, and switch the rule before the next round.
samples.goal: Practise colour and shape matching through a quick posting game with an immediate result after every choice.

guestPreview.imageAlt: Three colourful paper creatures being fed matching paper cards.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Use large paper cards that cannot be swallowed. An adult prepares any openings that need scissors.

background.alt: A colourful creature café Mission Wall

missions.title: Make three hungry creatures
setupSteps: Give each cup or bag a different coloured face.
An adult prepares one wide posting opening on each creature.
missions.sayThis: These creatures are hungry. Which colours should they eat?
missions.childChallenge: Choose each creature's colour and draw its funniest hungry face.
missions.tidyUp: Cap the markers before making the food cards.

missions.title: Feed the matching colours
setupSteps: Draw six large colour cards on paper scraps.
Mix the cards in one pile.
missions.sayThis: Feed every card to the creature with the same colour.
missions.childChallenge: Post all six cards, checking each match before letting go.
missions.tidyUp: Tip the cards back into one starting pile.

missions.title: Switch the feeding rule
setupSteps: Add a circle, stripe, or dot to each food card.
missions.sayThis: New rule: feed by the mark instead of the colour.
missions.childChallenge: Choose the new rule, feed every creature again, then catch one silly parent mistake.
missions.tidyUp: Store the cards inside one creature for another round.

samples.title: Mystery Touch Detective: Feel, Match & Reveal
samples.description: Reach into a mystery bag, describe one hidden object, and match it before the big reveal.
samples.goal: Build focused observation and descriptive language by identifying familiar objects without looking.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A child feeling a hidden object inside a colourful mystery bag.
guestPreview.safetyNote: An adult chooses clean, large, unbreakable objects with no sharp edges or choking hazards.

missions.title: Hide five mystery objects
setupSteps: Choose five safe objects with different textures or shapes.
Place them in the bag without showing the child.
missions.sayThis: Your detective hand can look without using eyes.
missions.childChallenge: Reach in, choose one object, and keep it hidden while feeling every side.
missions.tidyUp: Keep the mystery bag on the floor or a low table.

missions.title: Collect three touch clues
setupSteps: Draw simple clue marks for hard or soft, smooth or bumpy, and round or straight.
missions.sayThis: Tell me three clues before you make your guess.
missions.childChallenge: Describe the hidden object, point to matching clue marks, and guess what it is.
missions.tidyUp: Return each revealed object beside the bag.

missions.title: Become the mystery maker
setupSteps: Let the child secretly choose one safe object for the bag.
missions.sayThis: Now you give the clues and I will solve your mystery.
missions.childChallenge: Guide the grown-up with three touch clues without saying the object's name.
missions.tidyUp: Count all five objects back to their usual places.

samples.title: Sticker Treasure Route: Design, Follow & Deliver
samples.description: Draw a simple room map, build a sticker route, and follow it to complete three real-world deliveries.
samples.goal: Turn drawing and stickers into an active navigation challenge with planning, movement, and visible progress.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A hand-drawn treasure map with a bright sticker route connecting three room landmarks.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Choose safe, reachable landmarks away from stairs and doors. Keep stickers off floors where they could cause slips.

missions.title: Draw three room landmarks
setupSteps: Place the paper on a table.
Choose three safe landmarks such as the sofa, table, and toy basket.
missions.sayThis: Can you draw a simple mark for each real place?
missions.childChallenge: Draw the three landmarks and point from each drawing to its real match in the room.
missions.tidyUp: Keep the marker beside the map.

missions.title: Build the sticker road
setupSteps: Choose which landmark comes first, second, and last.
Place the first sticker at the starting point.
missions.sayThis: Add one sticker at a time until the road reaches every place.
missions.childChallenge: Build a continuous route, adding a bend, bridge mark, or stop sign of your choice.
missions.tidyUp: Return unused stickers to one sheet or small bowl.

missions.title: Follow and test the route
setupSteps: Choose three soft objects as treasures.
Place one treasure at the map's starting point.
missions.sayThis: Follow your map and deliver one treasure at every stop.
missions.childChallenge: Complete the route, repair any confusing part, then guide a grown-up through your improved map.
missions.tidyUp: Return the treasures and save or recycle the map.

samples.title: Sticker Shape Detective: Match, Count & Make a Pattern
samples.description: Cover matching shapes, fill counted spaces and make your own sticker pattern. Parent draws the sheet first, then checks in at the end.
samples.goal: Practise recognising shapes, counting one object at a time and continuing a simple pattern.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A paper sheet with matching shapes, counted coloured dots and a repeating sticker pattern.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Use large stickers or crayon dots instead of loose beans. Keep backing paper away from mouths. Parent draws the sheet before handing it over.

background.alt: A paper sheet with matching shapes, counted coloured dots and a repeating sticker pattern.

missions.title: Find the matching shapes
setupSteps: Parent draws three big circles and three big squares, mixed across a sheet.
Show one circle and one square. Leave large stickers within reach.
missions.sayThis: Can you find every circle?
missions.childChallenge: Put a sticker or crayon dot in each circle. Easier: use only two shapes. Harder: add triangles and match each shape to a different colour.
missions.tidyUp: Keep all backing paper in one pile.

missions.title: Give each box its number
setupSteps: Draw three boxes with 1, 2 and 3 dots at the top; use 4 and 5 for a harder round.
missions.sayThis: One sticker for each dot. Shall we count them as you place them?
missions.childChallenge: Fill each box with the matching number of stickers or crayon dots. Touch and count each mark once; check your own boxes.
missions.tidyUp: Keep unused stickers on their sheet.

missions.title: Make a repeating sticker trail
setupSteps: Start a red-blue-red-blue pattern with stickers or marker dots.
missions.sayThis: What comes next? Now make a pattern for me.
missions.childChallenge: Continue the pattern for six more marks. Easier: copy the two-colour pattern. Harder: invent a three-part pattern and leave a gap for a parent to solve.
missions.tidyUp: Save the finished sheet and put away the marker.

samples.title: Make a Wiggly Paper Snake
samples.description: Join paper loops into a snake, give it a face and extend its body with a repeating colour pattern. Parent cuts the pieces first and helps with the first loop.
samples.goal: Practise joining pieces, following a colour sequence and checking how a handmade object moves.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A green and yellow paper-chain snake with a drawn face and a long looping body.
materials: coloured paper strips and a paper head (adult-precut)
guestPreview.safetyNote: An adult cuts strips about 3 cm wide and 15 cm long, plus one large head shape. Use a glue stick, not staples. Do not wrap the chain around a neck.

background.alt: A green and yellow paper-chain snake with a drawn face and a long looping body.

missions.title: Connect the first three loops
setupSteps: Set out eight adult-cut strips in two colours and the precut head.
Help the child glue the first strip into a ring. Thread the next strip through it before closing.
missions.sayThis: Can you link a new loop through this one?
missions.childChallenge: Connect three loops. Hold each glued join briefly. Easier: parent holds the loop open. Harder: join the next two without help.
missions.tidyUp: Close the glue stick whenever you pause.

missions.title: Give your snake a face
setupSteps: Place the large precut head beside the chain.
Parent helps glue its back to the end loop.
missions.sayThis: What kind of face will your snake have?
missions.childChallenge: Draw two eyes and a mouth on the head. Add stripes or spots, then lift the head gently to see the body follow.
missions.tidyUp: Put the marker cap back on.

missions.title: Grow and test its patterned tail
setupSteps: Set the remaining strips in a reachable pile.
missions.sayThis: Green, yellow, green... which colour comes next?
missions.childChallenge: Add five loops in a repeating colour pattern. Check and fix any colour that breaks the pattern, then gently wiggle the finished snake along the table. Harder: create a three-colour tail.
missions.tidyUp: Let the joins dry flat, close the glue and collect paper scraps.

samples.title: Build a Standing Paper Dinosaur
samples.description: Decorate a dinosaur, fit its body into cardboard legs and adjust it until it stands. Parent prepares all cuts and helps with fitting; the child chooses the colours and tests the balance.
samples.goal: Make a recognisable dinosaur and investigate how leg placement changes its balance.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A decorated green paper-plate dinosaur standing on two short cardboard-roll legs.
materials: paper plate body and cardboard-roll legs (adult-precut)
guestPreview.safetyNote: An adult cuts a plate in half, prepares a head and tail with tabs and slots in the body, and cuts a clean cardboard roll into two short legs with top slots. Adult checks all edges before play; no child cutting is required.

background.alt: A decorated green paper-plate dinosaur standing on two short cardboard-roll legs.

missions.title: Design the dinosaur body
setupSteps: Set out the precut plate body, head and tail with crayons or markers.
Parent demonstrates how the pieces will look together.
missions.sayThis: Will your dinosaur have spots, stripes or both?
missions.childChallenge: Decorate the body and draw a large eye on the head. Easier: colour freely. Harder: make a repeating spot or stripe pattern.
missions.tidyUp: Cap markers before starting to build.

missions.title: Fit the head and tail
setupSteps: Parent holds the body and shows where the head and tail tabs fit.
missions.sayThis: Which piece is the head? Which side needs the tail?
missions.childChallenge: Slide the prepared tabs into their slots, with parent help if needed. Check that the face points away from the tail and the parts stay attached.
missions.tidyUp: Keep the two leg pieces together for the next step.

missions.title: Make it stand and test its balance
setupSteps: Parent helps slide the body into the two slotted cardboard legs on a low table.
missions.sayThis: What happens if its legs are too close together?
missions.childChallenge: Stand the dinosaur on a flat surface. Move the legs a little farther apart with a parent and compare. Once it stands, arrange a paper home around it. Harder: explain which leg position worked best.
missions.tidyUp: Store the dinosaur upright and collect spare paper pieces.

samples.title: Build a Paper Bridge That Holds a Toy
samples.description: Bridge a gap with paper, fold a stronger road and test whether your toy car can cross. Parent sets up the books, then returns to compare the child's designs.
samples.goal: Discover how folding changes the strength of paper by comparing two bridge designs.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A pleated paper bridge between two books carrying a small toy car.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Keep books and bridges on a low table or floor. Use a lightweight toy suited to the child's age; never use the bridge to support a person.

wallScene.title: Build a Paper Bridge That Holds a Toy

background.alt: A pleated paper bridge between two books carrying a small toy car.

missions.title: Try a flat paper road
setupSteps: Place two books the same height about 10 cm apart on the floor.
Lay one sheet across the gap.
missions.sayThis: Do you think this flat road can hold the car?
missions.childChallenge: Predict, then place the car in the middle gently and notice what happens. Parent helps if the sheet slips; there is no need to make it work yet.
missions.tidyUp: Put the car beside the books between tests.

missions.title: Fold a stronger bridge
setupSteps: Set out the second sheet.
Show how to fold a strip forward and back like a paper fan; a parent can start the first two folds.
missions.sayThis: What could these folds change?
missions.childChallenge: Make several folds across the sheet, then lay it across the same gap. Easier: parent makes folds and child opens the fan. Harder: try a different fold width.
missions.tidyUp: Keep both paper designs so you can compare them.

missions.title: Test, compare and improve
setupSteps: Use the same books, gap and car for both designs.
missions.sayThis: Which road bends less? How can you tell?
missions.childChallenge: Try the car on each bridge. Choose the better design and change just one thing, such as narrowing the gap, before testing again. Describe what changed.
missions.tidyUp: Return the car and books and recycle or save the bridges.

samples.title: Fold-and-Flip Funny Creatures
samples.description: Fold a paper flap, draw a small creature and open it to reveal a surprisingly long mouth or body. Parent demonstrates one fold, then the child draws and invents more versions.
samples.goal: Explore how a fold changes a picture while planning and drawing an original creature.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A folded paper creature opening to reveal a long colourful mouth.
guestPreview.safetyNote: Use paper and washable drawing tools only; no scissors are needed. Keep marker caps together and away from mouths.

background.alt: A folded paper creature opening to reveal a long colourful mouth.

missions.title: Make a paper picture flap
setupSteps: Fold a sheet in half, then fold the upper flap back to make a zigzag opening.
Parent demonstrates once and leaves the second sheet for another design.
missions.sayThis: Close it, open it. Where will your creature hide?
missions.childChallenge: Practise opening and closing the flap. Draw two small guide marks that meet when it is shut. Easier: parent prepares both folds. Harder: make your second fold yourself.
missions.tidyUp: Keep the paper flat on the table.

missions.title: Draw the closed creature
setupSteps: Keep the folded flap shut with its edges lined up.
missions.sayThis: A tiny mouth now... what might be hiding inside?
missions.childChallenge: Draw a face across the closed fold, with its mouth touching both edges. Add eyes, ears or horns. Try a second creature with a different expression if you have time.
missions.tidyUp: Keep the markers on the table beside the paper.

missions.title: Open, reveal and invent another
setupSteps: Open the flap slowly to see the blank space inside.
missions.sayThis: How long can its mouth or body become?
missions.childChallenge: Join the mouth lines through the hidden space, add big teeth or a colourful tongue and close it to test the surprise. Make another version on the second sheet, or add a pattern inside. Show a parent how the picture changes.
missions.tidyUp: Cap markers, keep favourite creatures and recycle spare paper.

samples.title: Carry the Sock: Balance, Walk & Try Again
samples.description: Carry a soft sock on a spoon between two cushion stations, then change your route and try again. Parent clears the floor and stays nearby while the child walks.
samples.goal: Practise controlled walking and hand balance, adjusting speed when a soft object slips.

guestPreview.imageAlt: A soft rolled sock resting on a large spoon beside two floor cushion stations.
materials: one loosely rolled pair of socks
guestPreview.safetyNote: Use a large blunt serving spoon and soft socks. Walk only on a clear, flat, non-slip floor; cushions mark stations and are not for climbing. An adult stays nearby.

background.alt: A soft rolled sock resting on a large spoon beside two floor cushion stations.

missions.title: Find your balancing grip
setupSteps: Place two cushions about three walking steps apart on a clear floor.
Put the soft sock on the bowl of the spoon.
missions.sayThis: Can your sock stay on while you stand still?
missions.childChallenge: Try holding the spoon with two hands, then one. Find a grip that keeps the sock steady. Easier: use both hands for the whole activity.
missions.tidyUp: Keep the cushions flat and clear of doorways.

missions.title: Carry it between two stations
setupSteps: Start beside one cushion and walk toward the other.
missions.sayThis: Slow steps or fast steps: which helps your sock stay on?
missions.childChallenge: Carry the sock there and back three times, walking slowly. If it drops, stop, pick it up and continue; no score or timer is needed.
missions.tidyUp: Place the spoon on a cushion whenever you pause.

missions.title: Change one thing and try again
setupSteps: Parent moves one cushion a step sideways to make a gentle turn.
missions.sayThis: What changes when your route bends?
missions.childChallenge: Follow the new route there and back. Try slower turns or a different grip and notice which helps. Harder: pause halfway for three counts without dropping the sock.
missions.tidyUp: Return the spoon to the kitchen and put away the socks and cushions.
